{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./pism_test1.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --ntasks=64          -> -n 64
#   --cpus-per-task=1    -> -c 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=64 -> best-effort by requesting -N 1 with -n 64
#
# NOTE: No Slurm time limit was specified; none is set for Flux.
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 64 -c 1 --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=... not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output/--error not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: stdout/stderr handling follows Flux defaults unless configured at submission.

  # NOTE: Slurm -p c6gn not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the c6gn partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --exclusive not translated.
  # Performance implication: without exclusive-node allocation, the job may share the node with other jobs, potentially reducing performance.

  spack load pism@1.1.4 %gcc /cijv4kn
  export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
  export OMP_PLACES=cores

  # Slurm used: srun ...
  flux run -n 64 -c 1 /usr/bin/time -f "real:%e" pismv -test B -Mx 61 -Mz 11 -ys 422.45 -y 25000 &> pismv.out
fi
"
}
